correctness.rationale: The recurrence yields \(AD-B^2=8\), the exact mod-\(48\) cycle \((1,3,17,3)\), pairwise coprimality, and \(M=AD\equiv17\pmod{48}\). Even \(K\) removes the parity obstruction. At primes dividing \(B\), all forms are \(1\); at primes dividing \(M\), their residues are \(1,-1/6,-6\); at every other prime \(\ell\ge5\), at most three parameter residues are forbidden; the prime \(2\) is handled separately. Thus every prime is covered without finite enumeration. Direct product expansion proves Korselt divisibility \(p_i-1\mid N-1\) whenever the three values are prime. Dickson is used only as an explicitly unproved hypothesis for infinitude. A standalone exact test covers 17 even indices, 37 primes, all parameter residues and a triple of genuine primes at \(n=2\). The infinite proof does not depend on the finite tests.

value.rationale: The exact three-prime existence gap left by the new Korselt characterization is natural and substantive: a congruence parametrization may conceal a fixed-prime obstruction, including at primes dividing its recurrence coefficients. The theorem eliminates all such local obstructions for every even index by exact structural identities, and makes a conditional infinity statement for each fixed index rather than a one-off parametric example. This is an all-index mathematical boundary result, not a relabelled finite calculation or an unconditional solution of Dickson.
